set.tovw: Paper cash thrown into the Fox River 1904; nothing recoverable
set.pl: Fox River by the Dousman mill (Dousman St crossing), Green Bay; pin is near the west bank, crossing not yet fixed
set.st: 19 May 1904: Joseph Doehm hanged himself at his Green Bay home. His note said relatives were after his money, so he had thrown it, $3,000-$4,000 in cash, into the Fox River near the Dousman mill. The story ran on the state wire to 25 May; no search or recovery was reported. Paper money in the river: nothing recoverable. Pin is approximate, near the west bank. Independent listing: Green Bay (WI gazetteer 1891 and 1905).
set.t: Look-only: paper cash in an urban river, nothing recoverable. Record only.

src: Milwaukee Daily News, 20 May 1904, p. 2 (newspapers.com 1298962119): money thrown in the Fox River near the Dousman mill

tw-wi-blackhawk-jaeger-1923.st: The Baraboo Republic (9 Aug 1923) dates the killing to 2 Aug and calls him a 'wealthy Blackhawk hermit'; the Reedsburg Times-Press (30 Aug 1923) puts him in a shack off the main road, a farmer of the town of Franklin, 'locally supposed to keep large sums of money about his premises'.
src: Baraboo Republic, 9 Aug 1923, p. 2 (newspapers.com 867636984), and 30 Aug 1923, p. 8

set.pl: Short St, Minonk (1940 census: next door to nephew John); 1930 house on Mary St; street not yet fixed on a map, pin on the village

tw-il-eureka-onnen-henhouse.t: Census: in 1930 he owned a house on Mary St, Minonk; in 1940 he lived on Short ('Shont') St next door to nephew John, the family home where he died. In-town house lot: look-only.
src: US census 1930 and 1940, Minonk, Woodford Co., IL (Henry Onnen household)
